findings.title: Journal search with an apostrophe crashes the server (search text pasted into SQL)
findings.expected: Searching O'Brien lists the entry containing O'Brien
findings.actual: GET /api/journal?q=O'Brien returns 500 (backend/routers/journal.py builds the LIKE clause with an f-string), and the page shows only 'Could not load the journal.' even though a matching entry exists
findings.evidence: {"alerts":["Could not load the journal."],"text":["Journal","The latest notes from across the garden, newest first.","Write in a plant's journal","Search","Clear search","Could not load the journal.","Garden Log · a journal for one garden"],"pageErrors":[]} | {"alerts":["Could not load the journal."],"text":["Journal","The latest notes from across the garden, newest first.","Write in a plant's journal","Search","Clear search","Could not load the journal.","Garden Log · a journal for one garden"],"pageErrors":[]}

findings.title: Journal search treats _ and % as wildcards and matches every entry
findings.expected: Searching '_' matches only entries or plant names that contain an underscore (none here)
findings.actual: '5 entries match' and every entry is listed, because the term goes into LIKE without escaping
findings.evidence: {"results":"5 entries match","nonMatching":["Double click test 1794500962940","Met O'Brien \"x\" at the fence","Tied the stems to canes.","First flowers opened; watered deeply.","Thinned the seedlings."]} | {"results":"5 entries match","nonMatching":["Double click test 1794500962940","Met O'Brien \"x\" at the fence","Tied the stems to canes.","First flowers opened; watered deeply.","Thinned the seedlings."]}
